newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt up, focus on Brazil, Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt up, focus on Brazil, Mexico.

text.p: A steep rise in the U.S. Treasury market -- which pushed the 30-year bond yield to 6.68 percent, its lowest level since April 4 at 6.66 percent -- sent LDC debt sharply higher at afternoon, with Argentina and Venezuela posting the biggest gains, traders said.
"Prices are basically trading up with the (long U.S. Treasury) bond," said one emerging markets debt trader at a major U.S. investment bank.
At 1600 EST/2000 GMT, Argentine FRBs ARFLC05=RR were 1-5/8 higher at 81-7/8 bid and Venezuelan pars VZ675C20=RR were 1-7/8 firmer at 70-1/2 bid.
Sources said emerging market debt instruments rose in line with U.S. Treasuries after news of a drop in consumer confidence and a more moderate than expected rise in the employment cost index (ECI).

Earlier today, the U.S. Labor Department said the ECI rose by 0.6 percent in the third quarter, down from 0.8 percent in the second quarter, and the Conference Board reported that the index of U.S. consumer confidence fell to 106.2 in October from a revised reading of 111.8 in September.
Although emerging market debt instruments lagged Treasuries early in the day, sources said there was some good buying in late afternoon.

"We were lagging earlier in the day but we are now seeing some decent buying on the back of the strength of Treasuries and on the turnaround in equities in Brazil," said a head trader at a major Wall Street firm.
However, the source noted that most of the trading action was in Latin American debt.
Mexican UMS-26 bonds MXUMS=RR were one percentage point stronger at 98-5/8 bid and Brazilian "C" bonds were 1-1/8 firmer at 68-3/4 bid.
Elsewhere, Russian Vneshekonombank dollar loans RUVNUSLNS=RR were one percentage point higher at 72-3/4 and Vnesh mark loans RUVNDMLNS=RR were 5/8 weaker at 76 bid.
